title: Lexus LFA vs Nissan GT-R: The Difference Nobody Explains
description:
Two Japanese supercars, both aimed at the same racetrack, the Nürburgring. One has a naturally aspirated V ten that screams to nine thousand r p m. The other has a twin-turbo V six and all-wheel drive. One was built in five hundred copies. The other in about forty-eight thousand. And at the Nürburgring, the cheaper car's best version was faster. This is the real difference between the Lexus LFA and the Nissan GT-R. Here is the twist. The LFA cost three hundred seventy-five thousand dollars new. The GT-R's launch price was around seventy thousand. By our arithmetic, the LFA cost more than five times as much. Yet according to Wikipedia, the GT-R Nismo's claimed Nürburgring lap beat the LFA's, and its engines were built by hand, one craftsman at a time. Let us go through the numbers, and where the sources disagree.

Every figure in this video comes from a published source, listed below.
